title: is_numeric() cannot change the result after is_int() narrowed the same operand

ground_truth.statement: is_int($c) is true for every int and is_numeric() is true for every int, so the right operand of the && never changes the value of the whole condition: classify() returns the same string as a version without the second call would, for every input.

allowed.reason: Same root cause reported under the && rule: left operand evaluates, right operand is always truthy. Correct, and Mago keeps the two rule classes apart.

notes: The claim is the redundancy of the second operand. PHPStan and Psalm both report it as a redundant condition on the function call; Mago reports the same fact as redundant-type-comparison plus redundant-logical-operation. The first draft of this expectation guessed a mago code that does not exist in mago 1.57.0 (the vocabulary is in crates/analyzer/src/code.rs); the claim was not changed, only its spelling.
